Eva Geller, a 90-year-old Jewish Holocaust survivor who escaped Nazi persecution as a child, has died in a Sydney hospital from complications linked to injuries she suffered during the December 14, 2025, terrorist attack on a Jewish Hanukkah celebration at Australia's Bondi Beach.

Geller, who fled Romania during the Holocaust and lost numerous relatives to Nazi persecution, was among dozens wounded when two Islamic State-inspired gunmen opened fire on Jewish families celebrating Hanukkah.

Fifteen people were killed in the original massacre. Her death brings the reported toll to 16.

Following the attack, Geller spent months in and out of hospital. Doctors initially told her she would never walk again, but she defied their expectations, regained the ability to walk and lived to celebrate her 90th birthday.

Rabbi Aron Moss of Bondi's Nefesh Synagogue, which she attended, said that despite being largely bedridden, she maintained her positive outlook.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese condemned her death:

“Eva should have been able to celebrate Chanukah in peace and safety and instead, her life was changed forever by an act of terror and antisemitism.”

posts.text:
SAG-AFTRA has dropped thousands of members for not paying dues.

“I fell behind on my dues over a year ago,” Colton Little, who has had recurring roles on “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital,” tells Variety, saying he owes about $2,000. “I was going through a lot. It got to the point where I had to prioritize paying my dues or paying my rent.”

For the last six years, SAG-AFTRA has refrained from kicking out members who fall behind on their dues, given how hard it has been for actors to find work during a pandemic, multiple strikes and a severe downturn in production. But on Nov. 1, the union reimposed its pre-COVID policy that anyone who falls behind by 18 months or more will be terminated.
